title: Three-stage lemma pipeline for IMO 2026 Q6 (purely periodic consecutive differences)
intent: Prove the headline theorem of IMO 2026 Q6 — that a valid sequence's consecutive differences are purely periodic — by composing three independently stated lemmas, each taking the previous one's conclusion as an explicit hypothesis: prime supports stabilise, the admissible set becomes shift-invariant, and shift invariance upgrades to pure periodicity.

parent.name: main_theorem
parent.statement:
theorem main_theorem (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : IsValidSeq a) :
    ∃ T L : ℕ, 0 < T ∧ 0 < L ∧ ∀ n, a (n + T) = a n + L

children.name: exists_stable
children.statement:
theorem exists_stable (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : IsValidSeq a) :
    ∃ N, ∀ n, ∃ i ≤ N, (a i).primeFactors ⊆ (a n).primeFactors
children.closed_by: exact exists_stable_of a ha hbound hreal hminsub, after discharging hkill/hminsub/hreal/hbound from killed_early, exists_minMem_subset, trans_realized, prime_bound
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: there is a bound N such that every prime support contains the support of one of the first N terms

children.name: exists_period
children.statement:
theorem exists_period (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : IsValidSeq a)
    (hstab : ∃ N, ∀ n, ∃ i ≤ N, (a i).primeFactors ⊆ (a n).primeFactors) :
    ∃ L, 0 < L ∧ ∀ b, (Adm a b ↔ Adm a (b + L))
children.closed_by: self-contained proof: witness `∏ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), a i`, both directions of the `Adm` equivalence via the `key` gcd ↔ common-prime-divisor dictionary
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: there is a positive L such that admissibility is invariant under translation by L

children.name: main_of_period
children.statement:
theorem main_of_period (a : ℕ → ℕ) (ha : IsValidSeq a)
    (hper : ∃ L, 0 < L ∧ ∀ b, (Adm a b ↔ Adm a (b + L))) :
    ∃ T L : ℕ, 0 < T ∧ 0 < L ∧ ∀ n, a (n + T) = a n + L
children.closed_by: self-contained proof: `T` is the index where `a 0 + L` occurs (via `adm_enum`), then induction on `n` bounded on both sides by `succ_le_of_adm`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: there are positive T and L such that a (n + T) = a n + L for every n

applicability.goal_shape: An ∃-goal reached through a chain of strengthenings: each stage is a named theorem of the form `premise → conclusion`, and the conclusions link the stages (stability ⇒ shift-invariance ⇒ pure periodicity). The glue is a single nested application `exact lemma3 (lemma2 (lemma1))`.
applicability.use_when: the target property is the composition of a short sequence of intermediate properties, each expressible as a self-contained named theorem whose hypothesis is exactly the previous theorem's conclusion; each stage closes on its own (or from named siblings), so the glue carries no argument of its own.
applicability.avoid_when: the intermediate properties are not natural standalone statements (an inline `suffices` is cleaner), a stage needs shared notation or context that cannot be stated independently, or the chain is long enough that the composed glue becomes hard to read.

claims.claim: No closing-by-sorry token (`sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`) occurs in lines 599-705 of IMO2026/Q6/solution.lean.

The decomposition is a pipeline of depth 3: `main_of_period` takes `hper` (the conclusion of `exists_period`) as a hypothesis, `exists_period` takes `hstab` (the conclusion of `exists_stable`) as a hypothesis, and `exists_stable` has no stage hypothesis.
The authors label the three stages in comments: 'THE CRUX' above `exists_stable`, the stabilise-then-period remark above `exists_period`, and 'Pure-periodicity lemma P' above `main_of_period`.

metrics.how_counted: direct_lemmas and glue_lines match shape; stage_chain_depth counts the lemmas in the single pipeline main_of_period → exists_period → exists_stable; all three children are full human-written proofs, none closed by a single tactic or automation

consequences: Each stage becomes an independent, reusable theorem with an explicit hypothesis that the next-lower stage must discharge; a missed or mis-typed discharge is caught as a type error at the glue line. The glue carries no argument of its own — all the mathematical content lives in the three lemmas. Failure mode: a stage stated a little too strong or too weak silently breaks the chain, since the only contract between stages is the hypothesis (`hstab`, `hper`); a subtle mismatch does not produce a counterexample, only a type error at composition.
